## Interpretation and decisions for discussion

With the same sample, covariates and fixed effects, the reduced-form coefficient
equals the 2SLS coefficient times the first-stage coefficient, up to numerical
precision. The offer effects therefore reveal the same underlying variation;
they are not an independent robustness check of the attendance estimates.

The offer effect describes the consequences of receiving a main-stage offer at
any school in the fixed over-demanded set. Its causal interpretation relies on
the validity of the conditional lottery comparison, including the approximation
to exact offer probabilities, the control timing, and the relevant interference
assumptions. It does not require exclusion or monotonicity for the pooled binary
attendance treatment. The present exercise preserves, rather than independently
validates, the handoff's inference and covariate choices.

Interpreting the ratio as an attendance LATE additionally requires the IV
assumptions. School changes within the over-demanded set, or outside it, may affect
outcomes without changing the pooled attendance indicator. Reporting the reduced
form does not resolve that concern. Conditioning on realized attendance would not
identify always-takers or isolate a causal within-set switching effect.

The finalized panel does not contain offered-school identities, ranked school
lists, or school-specific assignment draws. The upstream records recovered here
supply observed offers and lists, but not simulation draws or counterfactual
enrollment. This notebook does not infer individual counterfactual switches from
cross-sectional differences in realized destinations.

The generated appendix table reports the reduced forms with SEs and significance
stars, matching the existing paper tables; confidence intervals remain available
in this report and the CSV. A short reference in Section V could explain the
findings and the distinct assumptions for offer and attendance effects. That
discussion remains subject to author review. The conditional score results are
kept separate. This notebook does not edit manuscript prose or appendix inputs.

## F02.4: ninth-grade composition and the lottery population

This extension preserves the finalized composition outcomes, school-grade
classification, unbalanced-panel estimator, universal base period, and
not-yet-treated comparisons. Its primary change is to restrict the composition
sample to ninth grade. Regions first adopt ninth grade in entering-class years
2017, 2018, 2019, or 2020. Consequently only the first three waves have supported
post-adoption comparisons, through 2019; the Metropolitan Region is a comparison
region, not a treated region with an identified post-adoption effect here.
All ninth grades are entry grades, so a comparison region has not yet adopted
SAE in any grade under the documented rollout calendar.

We report pointwise intervals from the handoff's region-clustered multiplier
bootstrap with 10,000 draws. These are **not** the paper's permutation-test
p-values. No significance stars or new rollout-randomization claims are made.
The small number of regions and uneven adoption waves remain relevant to
inference (F13–F14); this extension does not resolve those separate concerns.
All-grade estimates are reestimated as a numerical baseline, not substituted
for the paper's saved inference. The notebook does not change manuscript files.

### Composition inputs and specification

```{r f02-inputs}
if (!requireNamespace("did", quietly = FALSE) || packageVersion("did") != "2.1.2")
  stop("F02.4 requires did 2.1.2. Install in an isolated library and set R_LIBS_USER before starting R if needed.")
if (getRversion() != "4.5.1") stop("F02.4 preserves the handoff's R 4.5.1 runtime.")
s2_manifest <- manifest[endsWith(manifest$path_in_dropbox, "/section2/section2_panel.rds"), ]
s2_override <- Sys.getenv("SAE_ADVERSARIAL_COMPOSITION_PANEL")
s2_candidates <- if (nzchar(s2_override)) path.expand(s2_override) else c(
  file.path(task_home, "Dropbox", s2_manifest$path_in_dropbox),
  file.path(output_dir, "input", "section2_panel.rds"))
s2_available <- s2_candidates[file.exists(s2_candidates) & !is.na(file.info(s2_candidates)$size) & file.info(s2_candidates)$size > 0]
if (!length(s2_available)) stop("No readable finalized Section 2 panel.")
s2_file <- normalizePath(s2_available[1])
stopifnot(nrow(s2_manifest) == 1L, identical(unname(tools::md5sum(s2_file)), s2_manifest$md5),
          file.info(s2_file)$size == s2_manifest$bytes)
s2 <- data.table::as.data.table(readRDS(s2_file))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(s2, by = c("MRUN", "AGNO")))
f02_provenance <- data.frame(file = s2_file, bytes = file.info(s2_file)$size,
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(s2_file)), did_version = as.character(packageVersion("did")),
  reference_notebook_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum("finalized_design_v1/section2/section2_cs_did.Rmd")),
  bootstrap_draws = 10000L, seed = 20261018L)
write.csv(f02_provenance, file.path(output_dir, "f02_provenance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

composition_cells <- s2[, list(n_ent = .N, n_gpa = sum(!is.na(PRIOR_GPA_Z)),
  gpa_z = mean(PRIOR_GPA_Z, na.rm = TRUE), sh_prio = mean(PRIO)),
  by = list(yr = AGNO, rbd = RBD, grade = COD_NIVEL, region = REGION, G = DOOR + 1L)]
composition_cells[grade < 2L, gpa_z := NA_real_]
composition_cells[, cell_id := as.integer(factor(paste(rbd, grade, sep = "|")))]
stopifnot(data.table::uniqueN(composition_cells$cell_id) == 8891L)
region_school_map <- unique(s2[COD_NIVEL == 9L, list(RBD, REGION, G = DOOR + 1L)])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(region_school_map$RBD), setequal(region_school_map$RBD, od_schools))
f02_designs <- list(all_grades = composition_cells, ninth_grade = composition_cells[grade == 9L])
```

### Estimates, support, and aggregation

The estimator uses observed cells separately in each comparison year, following
the baseline's unbalanced-panel convention. We independently reconstruct every
supported post-adoption contrast from its four cell means and verify the
aggregation weights against `did::aggte(type = "simple")`. Support exports report
region identities, observed cells, entrants, GPA coverage, and the actual weight
of each post-adoption comparison. Baseline and follow-up membership can differ.

```{r f02-composition-estimates}
f02_fits <- f02_results <- f02_support <- f02_events <- f02_checks <- list()
for (design in names(f02_designs)) for (outcome in c("gpa_z", "sh_prio")) {
  label <- paste(design, outcome, sep = "_")
  cells <- f02_designs[[design]]
  d <- as.data.frame(cells[is.finite(get(outcome)),
    list(cell_id, yr, G, region, y = get(outcome))])
  set.seed(20261018L + match(label, c("all_grades_gpa_z", "all_grades_sh_prio", "ninth_grade_gpa_z", "ninth_grade_sh_prio")))
  fit <- did::att_gt(yname = "y", tname = "yr", idname = "cell_id", gname = "G",
    data = d, control_group = "notyettreated", panel = TRUE, allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE,
    base_period = "universal", anticipation = 0L, bstrap = TRUE, biters = 10000L,
    clustervars = "region", cband = FALSE, print_details = FALSE)
  agg <- did::aggte(fit, type = "simple", na.rm = TRUE)
  dyn <- did::aggte(fit, type = "dynamic", na.rm = TRUE, cband = FALSE)
  f02_fits[[label]] <- list(fit = fit, aggregate = agg, dynamic = dyn)
  # Replicate the package's group-mass construction from its processed data.
  dp <- fit$DIDparams
  mass_data <- if (dp$panel) dp$data[dp$data$yr == min(dp$tlist), ] else
    stats::aggregate(dp$data, list(dp$data$cell_id), mean)[, -1]
  k <- which(fit$group <= fit$t & is.finite(fit$att))
  masses <- vapply(fit$group[k], function(g) mean(mass_data$.w * (mass_data$G == g)), numeric(1))
  weights <- masses / sum(masses)
  stopifnot(abs(sum(weights) - 1) < 1e-10,
            abs(sum(weights * fit$att[k]) - agg$overall.att) < 1e-10)
  for (j in seq_along(k)) {
    i <- k[j]; g <- fit$group[i]; t <- fit$t[i]; b <- g - 1L
    tb <- cells[G == g & yr == b & is.finite(get(outcome))]
    tt <- cells[G == g & yr == t & is.finite(get(outcome))]
    cb <- cells[G > t & yr == b & is.finite(get(outcome))]
    ct <- cells[G > t & yr == t & is.finite(get(outcome))]
    manual <- mean(tt[[outcome]]) - mean(tb[[outcome]]) - mean(ct[[outcome]]) + mean(cb[[outcome]])
    stopifnot(abs(manual - fit$att[i]) < 1e-8)
    f02_support[[paste(label,g,t)]] <- data.frame(design, outcome, adoption_year = g,
      entry_year = t, baseline_year = b, event_time = t - g,
      treated_regions = paste(sort(unique(c(tb$region,tt$region))), collapse = ","),
      control_regions = paste(sort(unique(c(cb$region,ct$region))), collapse = ","),
      n_treated_regions = length(unique(c(tb$region,tt$region))),
      n_control_regions = length(unique(c(cb$region,ct$region))),
      treated_baseline_cells = nrow(tb), treated_followup_cells = nrow(tt),
      control_baseline_cells = nrow(cb), control_followup_cells = nrow(ct),
      treated_baseline_entrants = sum(tb$n_ent), treated_followup_entrants = sum(tt$n_ent),
      control_baseline_entrants = sum(cb$n_ent), control_followup_entrants = sum(ct$n_ent),
      treated_followup_missing_gpa = sum(tt$n_ent - tt$n_gpa),
      control_followup_missing_gpa = sum(ct$n_ent - ct$n_gpa),
      estimate = fit$att[i], se = fit$se[i], weight = weights[j], reconstruction_error = manual - fit$att[i])
  }
  scale <- if (outcome == "sh_prio") 100 else 1
  f02_results[[label]] <- data.frame(design, outcome, unit = if (scale == 100) "pp" else "SD",
    estimate = scale * agg$overall.att, se = scale * agg$overall.se,
    lower = scale * (agg$overall.att - qnorm(.975) * agg$overall.se),
    upper = scale * (agg$overall.att + qnorm(.975) * agg$overall.se),
    observed_cell_years = nrow(dp$data), schools_or_cells = length(unique(dp$data$cell_id)),
    last_supported_entry_year = max(fit$t[k]), supported_post_contrasts = length(k))
  f02_events[[label]] <- data.frame(design, outcome, event_time = dyn$egt,
    estimate = scale * dyn$att.egt, se = scale * dyn$se.egt,
    lower = scale * (dyn$att.egt - qnorm(.975) * dyn$se.egt),
    upper = scale * (dyn$att.egt + qnorm(.975) * dyn$se.egt))
}
f02_results <- do.call(rbind, f02_results)
f02_support <- do.call(rbind, f02_support)
f02_events <- do.call(rbind, f02_events)
# Published point estimates are checked at their displayed precision; bootstrap
# SEs use fresh recorded seeds and are not required to be byte-identical.
f02_checks <- data.frame(outcome = c("gpa_z", "sh_prio"),
  estimate = f02_results$estimate[f02_results$design == "all_grades"] / c(1,100),
  manuscript_display = c(-.149, .035))
f02_checks$matches <- round(f02_checks$estimate, 3) == f02_checks$manuscript_display
stopifnot(all(f02_checks$matches), all(is.finite(f02_results$se)))
write.csv(f02_results, file.path(output_dir, "f02_composition_effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(f02_support, file.path(output_dir, "f02_composition_support.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(f02_events, file.path(output_dir, "f02_composition_event_times.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(f02_checks, file.path(output_dir, "f02_baseline_reproduction.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
f02_inference_audit <- f02_support[, c("design", "outcome", "adoption_year", "entry_year",
  "n_treated_regions", "n_control_regions", "se", "weight")]
f02_inference_audit$finite_bootstrap_se <- is.finite(f02_inference_audit$se)
write.csv(f02_inference_audit, file.path(output_dir, "f02_inference_diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(f02_results, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(f02_support[f02_support$design == "ninth_grade",
  c("outcome", "adoption_year", "entry_year", "treated_regions", "control_regions",
    "treated_followup_cells", "control_followup_cells", "weight")], digits = 4)
```

The support export also flags group-time effects for which the bootstrap returns
no usable SE. In particular, the 2017 adoption wave compared with the 2019
entering class has one treated region and one comparison region. Its estimate is
retained in the baseline aggregation, but we make no separate precision claim
for that contrast. The aggregate intervals are finite; finite intervals do not
remove the few-region inference concern.

### Comparable characteristics and pre-offer geographic support

The two finalized panels use different GPA standardizations. We recover the
annual affine conversion from students linked to the same ninth-grade entry in
both panels, require its maximum residual to be below 1e-8, and express applicant
GPA on the **composition panel's national prior-year GPA scale**. This changes
units only; no outcome is used to estimate the conversion. We retain separate
labels for entrant income measured in the entry year and applicant income
measured in the application year, and export their disagreement rate in linked
records. Entrants' descriptive means weight students equally, unlike the
school-cell and group-time weights of the composition ATT.

To align geographic and cohort coverage without selecting on actual attendance,
we use all recorded pre-lottery over-demanded choices, including automatically
added continuity options. An applicant is in the supported group if she has at
least one such choice and **every** such choice is in a region whose treated
ninth-grade entry cohort contributes to the composition estimates. This is a
conservative list-based definition, not the applicant's residence. It cannot
establish that her access changed because of SAE. Actual offers and attendance
are not used to define this group.

```{r f02-population-inputs}
ninth_entrants <- s2[COD_NIVEL == 9L]
profile_panel <- data.table::as.data.table(data.table::copy(panel))
profile_panel[, ENTRY_YEAR := YEAR + 1L]
linked_profiles <- merge(ninth_entrants, profile_panel,
  by.x = c("MRUN", "AGNO"), by.y = c("MRUN", "ENTRY_YEAR"))
stopifnot(all(linked_profiles$RBD == linked_profiles$ENTRY_RBD))
gpa_conversion <- linked_profiles[complete.cases(PRIOR_GPA_Z, GPA8_Z), {
  m <- lm(PRIOR_GPA_Z ~ GPA8_Z)
  list(n_linked = .N, intercept = unname(coef(m)[1]), slope = unname(coef(m)[2]),
       maximum_residual = max(abs(resid(m))))
}, by = list(ENTRY_YEAR = AGNO)]
stopifnot(all(gpa_conversion$maximum_residual < 1e-8), all(gpa_conversion$slope > 0))
profile_panel <- merge(profile_panel, gpa_conversion, by = "ENTRY_YEAR", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyNA(profile_panel$slope))
profile_panel[, GPA_COMPOSITION := intercept + slope * GPA8_Z]
measure_alignment <- linked_profiles[, list(n_linked = .N,
  income_status_disagreements = sum(PRIO != PRIORITARIO, na.rm = TRUE),
  entrant_income_mean = mean(PRIO, na.rm = TRUE),
  applicant_income_mean = mean(PRIORITARIO, na.rm = TRUE)), by = list(ENTRY_YEAR = AGNO)]
write.csv(gpa_conversion, file.path(output_dir, "f02_gpa_scale_conversion.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(measure_alignment, file.path(output_dir, "f02_income_measure_alignment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

support_gt <- unique(data.table::as.data.table(f02_support)[design == "ninth_grade",
  list(G = adoption_year, ENTRY_YEAR = entry_year)])
support_region_year <- merge(unique(region_school_map[, list(REGION, G)]), support_gt, by = "G", allow.cartesian = TRUE)
stopifnot(!any(support_region_year$REGION == 13L), max(support_region_year$ENTRY_YEAR) == 2019L)
raw_choices <- readRDS(upstream_paths[1])$c1
app_keys <- profile_panel[, list(proc = YEAR, mrun = MRUN)]
raw_choices <- raw_choices[app_keys, on = c("proc", "mrun"), nomatch = 0]
od_choices <- unique(raw_choices[rbd %in% od_schools, list(MRUN = mrun, YEAR = proc, RBD = rbd)])
od_choices <- merge(od_choices, region_school_map, by = "RBD", all.x = TRUE)
od_choices[, ENTRY_YEAR := YEAR + 1L]
od_choices[, in_supported_region_year := paste(REGION, ENTRY_YEAR) %in%
  paste(support_region_year$REGION, support_region_year$ENTRY_YEAR)]
choice_support <- od_choices[, list(n_od_choices_including_continuity = .N,
  all_choices_supported = all(in_supported_region_year),
  any_choice_supported = any(in_supported_region_year),
  n_choice_regions = data.table::uniqueN(REGION)), by = list(MRUN, YEAR)]
profile_panel <- merge(profile_panel, choice_support, by = c("MRUN", "YEAR"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
profile_panel[is.na(all_choices_supported), `:=`(all_choices_supported = FALSE, any_choice_supported = FALSE)]
lottery_support_audit <- profile_panel[LOTTERY_SAMPLE == TRUE, list(n = .N,
  supported = sum(all_choices_supported),
  mixed_support = sum(any_choice_supported & !all_choices_supported),
  no_supported_choice = sum(!any_choice_supported),
  missing_od_choice_list = sum(is.na(n_od_choices_including_continuity))), by = ENTRY_YEAR]
write.csv(lottery_support_audit, file.path(output_dir, "f02_lottery_support_audit.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lottery_support_audit)
rm(raw_choices, od_choices, app_keys, linked_profiles)
invisible(gc())
```

### Entrant, applicant, and complier profiles

Complier characteristics are estimated anew, rather than copied from the
existing appendix table, whose upstream weighting code is not in the handoff.
For each sample and characteristic X, let q_s be the observed offer frequency
within hundredth score group s, and let pi_s be the offered-minus-nonoffered
attendance difference. We estimate the complier mean as

\[
\widehat\mu_C(X)=
\frac{\sum_s n_s\{\overline{DX}_{1s}-\overline{DX}_{0s}\}}
     {\sum_s n_s\{\overline D_{1s}-\overline D_{0s}\}}.
\]

This is the score-stratified analogue of the complier-weighting argument in
[Abdulkadiroglu et al. (2017), p. 1402](https://economics.mit.edu/sites/default/files/publications/Abdulkadiroglu%20et.%20al.%202017%20-%20Research%20design%20meet.pdf).
It uses population shares and first stages rather than weighting each stratum by
its instrument variance. It requires conditional offer validity and monotone
attendance responses; it does not identify students individually as compliers.
Rounded-score conditioning remains an approximation. Characteristics are
predetermined, and no individual is selected on realized attendance. Groups
without both offer arms are reported as unsupported and excluded from this
profile estimator only. We use each characteristic's observed sample.

The influence-function SE below accounts for estimated within-group offer
frequencies, conditional means, and empirical group masses; observations are
independent as in the lottery baseline. A weighted fixed-effect IV reconstruction
checks the point estimate. The estimator and SE are explicitly specified here;
these are not a claimed reproduction of the existing complier table. Neither
these profile weights nor the composition weights equal the main covariate-
adjusted outcome 2SLS weights in general.

```{r f02-population-profiles}
f02_profile_rows <- list()
f02_profile_overlap <- list()
profile_samples <- list(full = profile_panel[LOTTERY_SAMPLE == TRUE],
                        supported = profile_panel[LOTTERY_SAMPLE == TRUE & all_choices_supported == TRUE])
for (scope in names(profile_samples)) for (v in c("GPA_COMPOSITION", "PRIORITARIO")) {
  d <- data.table::copy(profile_samples[[scope]][!is.na(get(v))])
  d[, X_PROFILE := get(v)]
  d[, DX := D_OD * X_PROFILE]
  means <- d[, list(ns = .N, q = mean(OFFER),
    d1 = mean(D_OD[OFFER == 1]), d0 = mean(D_OD[OFFER == 0]),
    dx1 = mean(DX[OFFER == 1]), dx0 = mean(DX[OFFER == 0])), by = CHANCE_GROUP]
  supported_means <- means[q > 0 & q < 1]
  f02_profile_overlap[[paste(scope,v)]] <- data.frame(scope, characteristic = v,
    chance_group = means$CHANCE_GROUP, n = means$ns, offer_frequency = means$q,
    included = means$q > 0 & means$q < 1)
  keep <- d$CHANCE_GROUP %in% supported_means$CHANCE_GROUP
  n_dropped <- sum(!keep)
  d <- merge(d[keep], supported_means, by = "CHANCE_GROUP", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  first_stage <- sum(supported_means$ns * (supported_means$d1 - supported_means$d0)) / nrow(d)
  numerator <- sum(supported_means$ns * (supported_means$dx1 - supported_means$dx0)) / nrow(d)
  stopifnot(first_stage > 0)
  mu <- numerator / first_stage
  d[, psi_num := dx1 - dx0 + OFFER / q * (DX - dx1) - (1 - OFFER) / (1 - q) * (DX - dx0)]
  d[, psi_den := d1 - d0 + OFFER / q * (D_OD - d1) - (1 - OFFER) / (1 - q) * (D_OD - d0)]
  influence <- (d$psi_num - mu * d$psi_den) / first_stage
  se_mu <- sqrt(sum(influence^2)) / nrow(d)
  d[, iv_weight := 1 / (q * (1 - q))]
  check_iv <- feols(DX ~ 1 | CHANCE_GROUP | D_OD ~ OFFER, d,
    weights = ~iv_weight, vcov = "hetero", ssc = iv_ssc, fixef.rm = "none")
  stopifnot(abs(unname(coef(check_iv)[1]) - mu) < 1e-8, abs(mean(influence)) < 1e-8)
  scale <- if (v == "PRIORITARIO") 100 else 1
  f02_profile_rows[[paste(scope,v,"applicants")]] <- data.frame(scope, population = "Lottery applicants",
    characteristic = v, n = nrow(d), excluded_no_offer_overlap = n_dropped,
    mean = scale * mean(d$X_PROFILE), se = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_,
    implied_complier_share = first_stage)
  f02_profile_rows[[paste(scope,v,"compliers")]] <- data.frame(scope, population = "Estimated complier profile",
    characteristic = v, n = nrow(d), excluded_no_offer_overlap = n_dropped,
    mean = scale * mu, se = scale * se_mu,
    lower = scale * (mu - qnorm(.975) * se_mu), upper = scale * (mu + qnorm(.975) * se_mu),
    implied_complier_share = first_stage)
}
entrant_sets <- list(
  full = ninth_entrants[AGNO >= DOOR + 1L & AGNO <= 2022L],
  supported = ninth_entrants[paste(REGION, AGNO) %in% paste(support_region_year$REGION, support_region_year$ENTRY_YEAR)])
for (scope in names(entrant_sets)) for (v in c("PRIOR_GPA_Z", "PRIO")) {
  x <- entrant_sets[[scope]][[v]]; x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  f02_profile_rows[[paste(scope,v,"entrants")]] <- data.frame(scope, population = "Ninth-grade entrants",
    characteristic = if (v == "PRIO") "PRIORITARIO" else "GPA_COMPOSITION", n = length(x),
    excluded_no_offer_overlap = NA_integer_, mean = mean(x) * if (v == "PRIO") 100 else 1,
    se = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_, implied_complier_share = NA_real_)
}
f02_profiles <- do.call(rbind, f02_profile_rows)
write.csv(f02_profiles, file.path(output_dir, "f02_population_profiles.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(do.call(rbind, f02_profile_overlap), file.path(output_dir, "f02_profile_score_support.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(f02_profiles, digits = 4)
```

The supported entrant cohort includes all entrants, whereas lottery applicants
must satisfy the original eighth-grade enrollment and application-history rules
and have nondeterministic offers. Complier profiles are inferred under the
lottery assumptions. The composition design still measures a change in the
composition of entrants, not a change in each subgroup's admission probability.
Similarities between entrant changes and complier characteristics are descriptive
connections, not evidence that the students gaining access under SAE are lottery
compliers. No composition estimate is multiplied by an attendance LATE.

### Results and proposed interpretation

```{r f02-summary-values, include=FALSE}
f02_value <- function(outcome, column, digits = 3) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), f02_results[f02_results$design == "ninth_grade" &
    f02_results$outcome == outcome, column])
}
f02_profile_value <- function(population, characteristic, digits = 3) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), f02_profiles[f02_profiles$scope == "supported" &
    f02_profiles$population == population & f02_profiles$characteristic == characteristic, "mean"])
}
```

The ninth-grade composition effect is **`r f02_value("gpa_z", "estimate")` SD**
for prior GPA, with a pointwise 95% interval of
[`r f02_value("gpa_z", "lower")`, `r f02_value("gpa_z", "upper")`], and
**`r f02_value("sh_prio", "estimate", 2)` pp** for the low-income share, with an
interval of [`r f02_value("sh_prio", "lower", 2)`,
`r f02_value("sh_prio", "upper", 2)`]. Both point estimates have the same
direction as the all-grade baseline. The low-income interval includes zero;
the restricted analysis does not reproduce the baseline's precision. It also
changes the supported regions, entry years, and aggregation weights.

There are `r format(sum(lottery_support_audit$supported), big.mark = ",")`
lottery applicants in the supported region-cohort window before profile-specific
missingness and overlap restrictions, compared with
`r format(nrow(entrant_sets$supported), big.mark = ",")` observed ninth-grade
entrants. On the common GPA scale, the entrant mean is
`r f02_profile_value("Ninth-grade entrants", "GPA_COMPOSITION")` SD, the
lottery-applicant mean is
`r f02_profile_value("Lottery applicants", "GPA_COMPOSITION")` SD, and the
estimated complier mean is
`r f02_profile_value("Estimated complier profile", "GPA_COMPOSITION")` SD.
The respective low-income shares are
`r f02_profile_value("Ninth-grade entrants", "PRIORITARIO", 2)`%,
`r f02_profile_value("Lottery applicants", "PRIORITARIO", 2)`%, and
`r f02_profile_value("Estimated complier profile", "PRIORITARIO", 2)`%.
Applicant and complier means use the same characteristic-specific overlap
sample; the score-support CSV identifies every omitted group. Income dates
differ as documented above.

These results connect the direction of the composition changes with the
observable characteristics of the lottery population. They neither identify
the reform's marginal entrants nor transport the attendance effect to them.
The author approved appendix tables reporting the ninth-grade estimates and
aligned profiles. The chunk below generates these tables for inclusion in the
access appendix. The author-approved main-text paragraph and table references are included after
the composition robustness discussion; no new estimand table or rollout
regression on college outcomes is proposed.

### Standalone appendix tables

The following exports contain complete table environments and follow the
manuscript's booktabs, spacing, and notes conventions. They are written here;
copying them into the manuscript is a separate, author-authorized step. The
main-text paragraph has also been approved and integrated separately.

```{r f02-appendix-tables, results='hide'}
f02_num <- function(x, digits) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
f02_ninth <- f02_results[f02_results$design == "ninth_grade", ]
stopifnot(f02_ninth$estimate[f02_ninth$outcome == "gpa_z"] < 0,
          f02_ninth$estimate[f02_ninth$outcome == "sh_prio"] > 0)
writeLines(c(
  "% Generated by analysis_for_adversarial_report.Rmd.",
  paste0("\\newcommand{\\SAENinthGradeGPADecline}{",
    f02_num(-f02_ninth$estimate[f02_ninth$outcome == "gpa_z"], 3), "}"),
  paste0("\\newcommand{\\SAENinthGradeIncomeIncrease}{",
    f02_num(f02_ninth$estimate[f02_ninth$outcome == "sh_prio"], 2), "}")),
  file.path(output_dir, "ninth_grade_macros.tex"))
f02_int <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
f02_row <- function(label, cells) paste0(label, " & ", paste(cells, collapse = " & "), " \\\\\n")
f02_float <- function(caption, label, alignment, body, note) paste0(
  "% Generated by analysis_for_adversarial_report.Rmd; do not edit numerical cells.\n",
  "\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\singlespacing\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.2}\n\\centering\n",
  "\\caption{", caption, "}\\label{", label, "}\n\\small\n",
  "\\begin{tabular*}{\\textwidth}{@{\\extracolsep{\\fill}}", alignment, "@{}}\n",
  "\\toprule\n", body, "\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular*}\n\\par\\smallskip\n",
  "\\begin{minipage}{\\textwidth}\\footnotesize\nNotes: ", note,
  "\n\\end{minipage}\n\\end{table}")
composition_body <- paste0(
  f02_row("Specification", c("\\shortstack{Prior-year GPA\\\\(SD)}", "\\shortstack{Low-income share\\\\(pp)}")),
  f02_row("", c("(1)", "(2)")), "\\midrule\n")
for (design in c("all_grades", "ninth_grade")) {
  r <- f02_results[f02_results$design == design, ]
  r <- r[match(c("gpa_z", "sh_prio"), r$outcome), ]
  digits <- c(3L, 2L)
  cells <- function(column) mapply(f02_num, r[[column]], digits, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  composition_body <- paste0(composition_body,
    f02_row(if (design == "all_grades") "All grades" else "Ninth grade", cells("estimate")),
    f02_row("", paste0("(", cells("se"), ")")),
    f02_row("95\\% confidence interval", paste0("[", cells("lower"), ", ", cells("upper"), "]")),
    f02_row("School-grade-years", f02_int(r$observed_cell_years)),
    if (design == "all_grades") "\\midrule\n" else "")
}
composition_note <- paste0(
  "The outcomes and estimator follow Table~\\ref{tab: alloc headline}. ",
  "The ninth-grade specification restricts the sample to ninth-grade entrants. ",
  "Both specifications use not-yet-treated school-grades, a universal pre-adoption base period, ",
  "no additional covariates, and the unbalanced-panel estimator described in Appendix~\\ref{app:access}. ",
  "Within comparisons, school-grade cells receive equal weight; group-time effects are aggregated by adoption-group size. ",
  "The all-grade and ninth-grade estimates cover supported post-adoption entering classes in 2017--2020 and 2017--2019, respectively. ",
  "For ninth grade, the Metropolitan Region supplies comparisons but has no identified post-adoption effect. ",
  "Observation counts include pre-adoption years from 2012. Region-clustered SE from 10,000 multiplier-bootstrap draws ",
  "are in parentheses; brackets report pointwise 95\\% intervals. All-grade point estimates reproduce the main table; ",
  "SE are recomputed with fresh draws. No permutation-test significance stars are reported. ",
  "The small number of regions remains a limitation for inference.")
writeLines(f02_float("Entering-Class Composition at Ninth-Grade Entry", "tab: ninth grade composition",
  "p{0.46\\textwidth}cc", composition_body, composition_note),
  file.path(output_dir, "appendix_ninth_grade_composition.tex"))

profile_order <- c("Estimated complier profile", "Lottery applicants", "Ninth-grade entrants")
profile_body <- paste0(f02_row("", c("\\shortstack{Students whose\\\\attendance depends\\\\on the offer}",
  "\\shortstack{Lottery\\\\applicants}", "\\shortstack{Ninth-grade\\\\entrants}")),
  f02_row("", c("(1)", "(2)", "(3)")), "\\midrule\n")
for (v in c("GPA_COMPOSITION", "PRIORITARIO")) {
  r <- f02_profiles[f02_profiles$scope == "supported" & f02_profiles$characteristic == v, ]
  r <- r[match(profile_order, r$population), ]
  digits <- if (v == "GPA_COMPOSITION") 3L else 2L
  profile_body <- paste0(profile_body,
    f02_row(if (v == "GPA_COMPOSITION") "Prior-year GPA (SD)" else "Low-income (\\%)", f02_num(r$mean, digits)),
    f02_row("", c(paste0("(", f02_num(r$se[1], digits), ")"), "", "")))
}
profile_body <- paste0(profile_body, "\\midrule\n")
for (v in c("GPA_COMPOSITION", "PRIORITARIO")) {
  r <- f02_profiles[f02_profiles$scope == "supported" & f02_profiles$characteristic == v, ]
  r <- r[match(profile_order, r$population), ]
  profile_body <- paste0(profile_body, f02_row(if (v == "GPA_COMPOSITION") "$N$, GPA" else "$N$, low-income", f02_int(r$n)))
}
excluded_profile <- function(v) f02_profiles$excluded_no_offer_overlap[
  f02_profiles$scope == "supported" & f02_profiles$population == "Lottery applicants" & f02_profiles$characteristic == v]
profile_note <- paste0(
  "The samples cover the regions and 2017--2019 entering cohorts contributing treated observations to ",
  "Table~\\ref{tab: ninth grade composition}. Lottery applicants are retained when every over-demanded school ",
  "on their pre-lottery list, including automatic continuity options, belongs to a supported region-cohort. ",
  "No restriction uses the realized offer or school attended. Columns (1) and (2) use the same observed-characteristic ",
  "sample and retain hundredth propensity-score groups containing both offer arms; this excludes ",
  f02_int(excluded_profile("GPA_COMPOSITION")), " applicants for GPA and ",
  f02_int(excluded_profile("PRIORITARIO")), " for income after removing missing characteristics. ",
  "Column (1) uses the complier-profile estimator described in Appendix~\\ref{app:ninth-grade-composition}; ",
  "heteroskedasticity-robust influence-function SE are in parentheses. Its $N$ is the estimation sample size, ",
  "not a count of identified compliers. Columns (2) and (3) are student-weighted means. ",
  "GPA is on the composition analysis's national prior-year scale; the lottery measure is converted using exact ",
  "year-specific affine relationships in linked records. Low-income status is measured in the application year ",
  "for applicants and compliers, and the entry year for entrants. ",
  "These profiles describe different populations and do not identify the students whose access changed under SAE.")
writeLines(f02_float("Entrants and Lottery Compliers in the Supported Ninth-Grade Cohorts",
  "tab: ninth grade profiles", "p{0.30\\textwidth}ccc", profile_body, profile_note),
  file.path(output_dir, "appendix_ninth_grade_profiles.tex"))
```

## F04.4: entrant counts and low-income composition

The count extension uses the finalized Section 2 entrant panel and the same
unbalanced-panel estimator as the composition results. Low-income entrants have
entry-year `PRIO == 1`; other entrants have `PRIO == 0`. The script verifies that
these flags have no missing or nonbinary values. All four outcomes share the
sample and aggregation weights, and count additivity is checked at the cell,
group-time, aggregate-effect, and aligned-bootstrap-draw levels.

The input records only positive-entry school-grade-years. Its missing cells
cannot distinguish zero entrants from missing records or a grade not operating.
We retain the original sample and do not impute zeros. The coverage audit counts
these unclassified omissions. The analysis therefore does not estimate effects
on the probability of having any entrants or national subgroup totals.

The table separates unbalanced-panel estimates and bootstrap intervals from
paired estimates and their studentized regional permutation tests. The latter
reuse the manifest-verified `intake_count.rds` schedules (2,999) for all counts and
`headline.rds` schedules (9,999) for the share. An optimized sufficient-statistic
implementation is checked against the baseline notebook's unchanged statistic
for the observed rollout and six saved schedules for every outcome. F13–F14's
estimator and few-region inference concerns remain open. The analysis does not
construct a pre-SAE applicant denominator.

To run just this extension from `code/`, use the same R library as above:

```bash
Rscript f04_entrant_counts.R
```

Set `SAE_PAPER_ROOT` to the directory containing `main.tex` and `tables/` to export
the generated table and numerical macros. Inputs are found in shared Dropbox or
`analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/input/` and checked against the manifest.
Results, support, input audits, verification checks, permutation statistics,
provenance, and region-level bootstrap archives are saved under
`analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/f04/`. The bootstrap covariance uses sample
second moments; `did`'s reported multiplier SEs use its IQR scaling.

```{r f04-counts}
source("f04_entrant_counts.R", local = new.env(parent = globalenv()))
f04_results <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "f04", "effects.csv"))
knitr::kable(f04_results[, c("label", "pre_mean", "estimate", "se", "lower", "upper",
                            "paired_estimate", "paired_jackknife_se", "p_ri")], digits = 3)
```

The low-income share rises, while the unbalanced-panel count intervals include
zero for both groups. Thus, a change in entrant composition is more firmly
supported than an increase in low-income entrant numbers. The paired low-income
count estimate and permutation p-value differ from the unbalanced-panel estimate
and interval; the table presents them separately rather than treating them as
interchangeable inference for one coefficient.

## F08: annual PACE rules and measurement audit

This section implements the annual-rule and measurement audit, followed by new
PACE-selection and school-attendance estimates. Academic qualification is
constructed only to the extent the scores and reference population permit;
unresolved cases are retained explicitly.
The published rules cover admission processes 2021--2026, including all processes
in the longer-follow-up tables (the last school-application cohort is reduced
when the follow-up window increases). The 2027 validity endpoint below concerns
2025 graduates; no 2027 admission outcomes enter these tables.

### Official rules

The annual thresholds are policy inputs, transcribed from the official documents
in `f08/sources/`. The academic alternatives are joined by **OR**. School history,
graduation, and the required examinations are additional conditions. Since 2023,
prehabilitation combines school history and the academic criterion; habilitation
also requires the specified examinations. Prior-cohort eligibility carried into
a later process must retain its original cohort rule, rather than being tested
against the threshold for the new graduating cohort.

```{r f08-rules}
# This chunk can run independently from code/ without the earlier estimations.
f08_dir <- file.path("analysis_for_adversarial_report_output", "f08")
dir.create(f08_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
f08_urls <- c(
  "https://acceso.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/2020.10.22_FINAL_OFERTA-PACE.pdf",
  "https://acceso.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/PACE-oferta-2022-27-10-21.pdf",
  "https://acceso.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/PACE-DEMRE-2023-26-10-22-1.pdf",
  "https://dfi.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/sites/114/2023/06/Rex3625-2023_aprueba-criterios-prehab-y-habilitacio%CC%81n-PACE2024.pdf",
  "https://acceso.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Oferta-Definitiva-202519-12-2024_compressed.pdf",
  "https://acceso.mineduc.cl/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/oferta-Definitiva-2026-291025UV_compressed-1.pdf"
)
f08_rules <- data.frame(
  admission_process = 2021:2026,
  new_graduation_cohort = 2020:2025,
  top_share = c(.15, .15, .20, .20, .25, .25),
  minimum_ranking = c(710, 749, 863, 851, 815, 830),
  ranking_scale = c(rep("PDT-era scale (150-850)", 2),
                    rep("PAES-era scale (approximately 100-1000)", 4)),
  academic_operator = "within-school Ranking percentile OR Ranking >= threshold",
  school_history = "Grades 11 and 12 in participating schools; graduate from a participating school",
  required_exams = c(rep("PDT reading + mathematics + history/social sciences OR sciences", 2),
    rep("Regular PAES reading + Mathematics 1 + history/social sciences OR sciences", 4)),
  valid_through = c(2021L, 2022L, 2024L, 2025L, 2026L, 2027L),
  incoming_carryover = c("None in annual guide", "None in annual guide", "None in annual guide",
    "2022 graduates retain 2023 prehabilitation/unused habilitation; complete exams if needed",
    "2023 graduates retain 2024 prehabilitation/unused habilitation; complete exams if needed",
    "2024 graduates retain 2025 prehabilitation/unused habilitation; complete exams if needed"),
  use_limit = c(rep("Corresponding annual process", 2),
    "One use across 2023 and 2024",
    rep("One use; enrollment at a PACE university consumes eligibility regardless of admission route", 3)),
  selection_score = c(rep("(0.8 Ranking + 0.2 NEM)*(1 + territory bonus) + preference bonus", 4),
    rep("(0.8 Ranking + 0.2 NEM)*(1 + territory bonus) + preference bonus + degree-type bonus", 2)),
  selection_conditions = "Eligible applicant; listed program with PACE vacancies; PPP ordering and program-specific requirements; selection differs from enrollment",
  source_file = c("pace2021.pdf", "pace2022.pdf", "pace2023.pdf", "resolution2024.pdf", "pace2025.pdf", "pace2026.pdf"),
  source_pages = c("3-5", "3-5", "3-5", "3-7 (REX 3625, 2023-06-29)", "6-11", "6-10"),
  effective_scope = paste("Admission", 2021:2026, "new graduates", 2020:2025),
  source_url = f08_urls,
  checked_on = "2026-10-19",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# The 2024 resolution explicitly restricts the percentile reference group to
# graduates satisfying its school-history condition (p. 3, footnote 1).
f08_rules$percentile_reference <- "Graduating school's official Ranking ordering; verify operational roster, ties and rounding before reconstruction"
f08_rules$percentile_reference[4] <- "Graduates satisfying school-history condition, ordered by official Ranking (REX 3625 p. 3 fn. 1); ties/rounding require verification"
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(f08_rules$admission_process),
          all(f08_rules$admission_process == f08_rules$new_graduation_cohort + 1L),
          all(file.exists(file.path(f08_dir, "sources", f08_rules$source_file))))
write.csv(f08_rules, file.path(f08_dir, "pace_rules_2021_2026.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

f08_rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(f08_rules)), function(i) {
  r <- f08_rules[i, ]
  valid <- if (r$valid_through == r$admission_process) as.character(r$admission_process) else
    paste0(r$admission_process, "--", r$valid_through)
  paste0(r$admission_process, " & ", r$new_graduation_cohort, " & ",
         100 * r$top_share, "\\% & $\\geq ", r$minimum_ranking, "$ & ", valid, " \\\\")
}, character(1))
f08_tex <- c(
  "% Generated by analysis_for_adversarial_report.Rmd, chunk f08-rules.",
  "\\begin{table}[!htbp]",
  "\\singlespacing\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.25}\\centering",
  "\\caption{PACE Academic Requirements by Admission Process}\\label{tab: pace annual rules}",
  "\\small\\begin{tabular}{ccccc}\\toprule",
  "Admission & Graduation & Within-school & Absolute Ranking & Valid admission \\\\",
  "process & cohort & top share & alternative & processes \\\\\\midrule",
  f08_rows,
  "\\bottomrule\\end{tabular}\\par\\smallskip",
  "\\begin{minipage}{\\textwidth}\\footnotesize",
  paste0("Notes: Each row describes a newly graduating cohort. The academic condition is the within-school ",
    "percentile of the official Ranking score or the absolute-score alternative. Scores use the 150--850 ",
    "scale in 2021--2022 and the approximately 100--1000 scale from 2023. Students must also attend ",
    "grades 11 and 12 and graduate from a participating school, and take reading, mathematics ",
    "(Mathematics 1 from 2023), and an elective in history/social sciences or sciences. From 2023, ",
    "school history and the academic condition establish prehabilitation; the required regular exams ",
    "establish habilitation. A previous cohort can retain eligibility in the following process, ",
    "subject to exam completion and the one-use condition, without being reassessed under the new ",
    "cohort's academic threshold. The 2024--2026 rules count enrollment at a PACE university as use ",
    "regardless of the admission track. The 2024 resolution defines the percentile reference group ",
    "as graduates meeting the school-history condition. Selection ranks eligible applications using ",
    "80\\% Ranking and 20\\% NEM, with territorial and preference-order bonuses; the 2025--2026 ",
    "guides also include degree-type bonuses. Eligibility does not imply application or selection."),
  paste0("Sources: Annual official guides for 2021--2023 ",
    "\\citep{paceRules2021,paceRules2022,paceRules2023}, Resolution 3625 of June 29, 2023 ",
    "for admission 2024 \\citep{paceRules2024}, and the 2025--2026 guides ",
    "\\citep{paceRules2025,paceRules2026}."),
  "\\end{minipage}\\end{table}"
)
writeLines(f08_tex, file.path(f08_dir, "appendix_pace_rules.tex"))
f08_paper_root <- Sys.getenv("SAE_PAPER_ROOT")
if (nzchar(f08_paper_root)) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(f08_paper_root, "main.tex")))
  file.copy(file.path(f08_dir, "appendix_pace_rules.tex"),
            file.path(f08_paper_root, "tables", "appendix_pace_rules.tex"), overwrite = TRUE)
}
knitr::kable(f08_rules[, c("admission_process", "new_graduation_cohort", "top_share",
                          "minimum_ranking", "valid_through")])
```

Resolution 4042/2026, pp. 4--5, updates Resolution 7447/2025 for **admission
2027** and explicitly preserves the latter's application to admission 2026.
Its consolidated 2027 text must not be used retroactively as the rule for all
2021--2026 cohorts. The original code cites this consolidation in a comment,
but does not implement an academic threshold in the PACE school/appearance chain.

### What the existing code actually measures

The archived source is commit `79fc4771123fadef963f5bcbb6b2e2b2f9b2a24f`,
`code/piece4/1_decompose_assignment.Rmd` (routes and pace chunks) and
`code/piece4/checks/92_pace_seat_chain.R`. These files were recovered read-only
from Git history, without checking out or changing the current branch.

- `L_PACE` is presence in a separate PACE application/selection file in
  2021--2023 OR at least one main-file preference with `tipo == "PACE"`.
  Missing matches are zero. This is record appearance, not a reconstructed
  academic-qualification measure or a documented universal eligibility flag.
- `S_PACE` additionally requires `ESTADO_PREF == 24` in at least one preference
  (or `estado == 24` on the processed main file). It measures recorded selection,
  not enrollment. Main-file and separate-file selections are reconciled with the
  assignment record in the archived script.
- `S_raw` links a student's unique school in a grade-12 performance record in
  admission year minus one to a school list inferred from **any** student at that
  school appearing in PACE records. The final school indicator is
  `S = S_raw | L_PACE`. Thus the student's own appearance overrides an absent
  school match. Nonappearing students without a unique school receive zero.
  Neither grade-11 attendance nor both-year official participation is checked.
- `S2` substitutes official school lists for 2022, 2023, and 2025, but still
  applies `| L_PACE`. Other years retain the derived school list. This is a
  partial sensitivity check, not an independent official school-history measure.
  The archived claim that official lists do not exist in the other years is
  incorrect: the ministry's PACE document registry also lists school-designation
  resolutions for those years. Independent rosters are extracted and linked below.
- The school/appearance/selection comparisons condition on on-time graduation,
  both compulsory scores, and a college application. Of 15,906 such applications
  in the 45,123-application mechanism frame, 15,392 remain in 1,069 strata with
  both offer statuses. This is a post-offer selected sample. It is not the full
  entrant population and is not the Section 3 attendance-IV sample.

`chain_run` first pools within-stratum arm rates with weights
`n_winner * n_loser / n`. It divides cumulative rates to obtain conditional
rates and substitutes the offer-arm rates in order. The contribution of step
`k` is the product of earlier offer-arm rates, the difference at step `k`, and
later no-offer-arm rates. Components sum to the final outcome difference. This
ordered accounting does not identify causal mediation. The total's SE clusters
by school/application year; component stars use 9,999 within-stratum offer
reshuffles, recomputing the accounting.

| Draft exhibit | Outcome and denominator | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Main table `tab:funnel_towards_assignment`, PACE row | PACE contribution to the admission step of the graduation/exam/application/selection sequence; 23,754 first-choice school applications from 2016--2019 at every horizon | A contribution in seats per 100 school applications, not the direct PACE-selection offer coefficient. Earliest selection determines the track. The imported horizon table and its notes were inspected; the exact updated horizon exporter is not present on this branch or in the recovered piece4 code, so this audit does not claim a new numerical reproduction. |
| Appendix `tab:section6_reconciliation`, Panel B | School link then PACE-record appearance; 15,392 on-time college applications | Decomposes appearance, not PACE admission. The first link is a proxy with an individual-record override; the second combines remaining requirements and application behavior. Archived two-link outputs match the displayed rounded values. |
| `tables/section6_pace_panel.tex` | School link, record appearance, PACE selection; same 15,392 applications | Three-link extension in `92_pace_seat_chain.R`; present in Skeleton but not currently included in the active manuscript. Its last link measures selection conditional on record appearance, not academic eligibility alone. |
| Appendix adjustment paragraph | PACE selection in the five-outcome family among on-time college applicants | Reports individual and family-adjusted randomization p-values; no new channel separation. |
| Appendix arm-rate and horizon-reconciliation tables | Any-track sequence rates and recorded assignment versus completion of the sequence | These do not estimate PACE academic eligibility; they clarify the broader funnel denominators. |

The older `code/4_pace_robustness.Rmd` (archive commit
`5f56f1d147757c1bad3f0899007737ef0c6c218f`) uses `is_pace`/raw `pace` at a
student's **first** admission process, excludes PACE outcomes, and excludes
ever-PACE schools for an earlier gender/DiD exercise. It is not the generator of
the current mechanism tables. Its `enrolled_pace` additionally matches enrolled
and PACE-selected program codes. Do not interchange that flag, first-process
timing, or enrollment outcome with the current piece4 record-appearance measure.

### DEMRE variable descriptions and source reconciliation

DEMRE's public portal, registration file B for admission 2026,
`Libro_CodigosADM2026_ArchivoB.xlsx`, cell A50/B50, defines `PACE` as
“Postulante Informado por el MINEDUC como alumno preseleccionado PACE”.
The original workbook (accented filename) is retained under `f08/sources/`.
This is an administrative preselection label. The description does not define
it as the score criterion alone or specify enough timing detail to equate it
automatically with final habilitation. The 2021 and 2026 score-file C dictionaries
were also inspected; the PACE flag is not defined there. The upstream construction has now been recovered (below), and shows that this
2026 dictionary cannot be used to interpret the harmonized flag in earlier years.
The active piece4 chain does not use the registration flag.

### Independent school rosters and new channel estimates (2026-10-19)

The ministry's PACE registry supplies school-designation resolutions for
2019--2024 and later amendments. Annual official school directories contain a
PACE indicator for 2022--2025. These are independent of students' applications.
`f08/sources/schools/official_pace_schools_2019_2025.csv` records the school year,
RBD, and source for every participating school. The 2019--2021 scanned resolutions
were extracted with local OCR; `ocr_corrections.csv` records corrections checked
against the original PDFs. The resulting counts are 574, 581, 580, 580, 638, 638,
and 651. The 2025 directory flags 650 schools; Resolution 30/2025 explicitly adds
RBD 268 as well, so the legal designation is included and the discrepancy retained.
Resolution 5702/2024 replaces RBD 10737 with 24856, consistent with the directory.
Source URLs are in `f08/sources/schools/urls.json`.

The upstream processing script was recovered from
`/Education - On going projects/Code/R/1_data_processing.Rmd` in the connected
Dropbox and preserved read-only as `f08/archive/1_data_processing_upstream.Rmd`.
This establishes a **definition change**, not just an ambiguous dictionary:

- Through 2022, `pace` is the original `P167` field. The supplied 2022 dictionary,
  sheet 1 row 363, calls this “Inscrito informado PACE”; row 369 separately defines
  `P081_1` as the PACE status at the time of the examination. Neither is defined as
  the academic criterion alone. In the observed 2021--2022 records, P167 is almost
  universal among registrants graduating from participating schools and includes
  many students below even an optimistic academic cutoff.
- For 2023--2025, upstream lines 1102--1105 **replace** `pace` with
  `ifelse(!is.na(codigo_carrera_pace_1), "PACE", "")`. Line 1353 then constructs
  `is_pace` from that label. It records a PACE program at the first preference
  position. A student with a PACE preference only at a later position can have
  `is_pace == 0`, including some PACE selections.
- `assigned_pace` agrees exactly with any PACE preference having selection status
  24 in the recovered 2020--2025 panel. Selection is usable; the stored `pace` /
  `is_pace` variables must not be used as a common eligibility outcome.
- The 2021, 2023, and 2025 MINEDUC registrant-score files and dictionaries were
  recovered too. They do not contain a PACE eligibility variable. The separate
  DEMRE 2026 registration dictionary's preselection definition therefore cannot
  be attached to the harmonized `pace` column. The cached MRUN-linked 2026 data
  retain scores and any-track preference status, but omit the selection route.

All new statistical construction and estimation below is in this notebook.
`f08_extract_rds_columns.py` only reads selected columns from the 28 GB expanded
RDS without loading the entire object. The original files remain unchanged.
The common on-time estimation sample uses SAE applications in 2016--2020 and
college admission processes 2021--2025, with Section 3's chance-group design,
controls, and standard errors. The 2021 SAE cohort is excluded here because its
2026 PACE selection route is unavailable in the cached MRUN-linked data.
School records and academic-rule inputs are assembled through school year 2025 /
admission 2026 for the coverage audit. These are new estimates and do not reproduce
the archived first-choice mechanism sample or its ordered decomposition.

```{r f08-input-projection}
library(data.table)
library(jsonlite)
library(fixest)
setDTthreads(4)
f08_input <- file.path("analysis_for_adversarial_report_output", "input", "f08")
f08_dir <- file.path("analysis_for_adversarial_report_output", "f08")
f08_schools <- file.path(f08_dir, "sources", "schools")
f08_cache <- file.path(f08_input, "student_pace_2020_2025.rds")
if (!file.exists(f08_cache)) {
  projection <- fromJSON(file.path(f08_dir, "student_column_projection.json"),
                         simplifyVector = FALSE)
  coldir <- file.path(f08_input, "student_columns")
  status <- system2(Sys.getenv("PYTHON", "python3"),
    shQuote(c("f08_extract_rds_columns.py",
      file.path(f08_input, "data_students_2004_2025.rds"), coldir,
      file.path(f08_dir, "student_column_projection.json"))),
    stdout = file.path(f08_dir, "column_projection.log"), stderr = "")
  stopifnot(status == 0L)
  metadata <- fromJSON(file.path(coldir, "metadata.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)$value
  n_raw <- metadata[[2L]]$n
  year_raw <- readBin(file.path(coldir, "year.bin"), "double", n = n_raw, endian = "big")
  take <- which(year_raw >= 2020 & year_raw <= 2025)
  projected <- data.table(year = year_raw[take])
  rm(year_raw)
  for (i in names(projection)) {
    nm <- projection[[i]]
    if (nm == "year") next
    type <- metadata[[as.integer(i) + 1L]]$type
    if (type == 16L) {
      v <- readLines(file.path(coldir, paste0(nm, ".txt")))
      v[v == "__RDS_NA__"] <- NA_character_
    } else {
      v <- readBin(file.path(coldir, paste0(nm, ".bin")),
                   if (type == 14L) "double" else "integer", n = n_raw, endian = "big")
    }
    stopifnot(length(v) == n_raw)
    set(projected, j = nm, value = v[take])
    rm(v)
  }
  stopifnot(nrow(projected) == 1789837L,
            uniqueN(projected, by = c("mrun", "year")) == nrow(projected))
  saveRDS(projected, f08_cache)
  rm(projected)
}
# Preserve the entire national graduate reference population, not just lottery applicants.
f08_perf_cache <- file.path(f08_input, "performance_upper_2019_2023.rds")
if (!file.exists(f08_perf_cache)) {
  all_perf <- as.data.table(readRDS(file.path(f08_input, "panel_performance_2002_2023.rds")))
  upper <- all_perf[AGNO >= 2019 & COD_GRADO %in% c(3L, 4L) &
    COD_ENSE %in% c(310L, 410L, 510L, 610L, 710L, 810L, 910L),
    .(MRUN, AGNO, RBD, COD_ENSE, COD_GRADO, PROM_GRAL, SIT_FIN_R)]
  saveRDS(upper, f08_perf_cache)
  rm(all_perf, upper)
  gc()
}
```

```{r f08-build-channel-data}
library(data.table)
setDTthreads(4)
p<-'analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/input/f08'
s<-'analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/f08/sources/schools'
roster<-fread(file.path(s,'official_pace_schools_2019_2025.csv'))
perf<-readRDS(file.path(p,'performance_upper_2019_2023.rds'))
extra<-readRDS(file.path(p,'rendimiento_grades_2024_2025.rds'));setDT(extra)
perf<-rbindlist(list(perf,extra[AGNO>=2024 & COD_GRADO %in% c(3L,4L) & COD_ENSE %in% c(310L,410L,510L,610L,710L,810L,910L)]),use.names=TRUE)
rm(extra)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(roster, by=c('school_year','RBD')))
# Multiple distinct school records are retained as an ambiguous school, not resolved using PACE.
hist<-perf[,.(n_school=uniqueN(RBD[!is.na(RBD)]),RBD=if(uniqueN(RBD[!is.na(RBD)])==1L)unique(RBD[!is.na(RBD)])[1] else NA_integer_,passed=any(SIT_FIN_R=='P',na.rm=TRUE)),by=.(MRUN,AGNO,COD_GRADO)]
hist[,pace_school:=as.integer(paste(AGNO,RBD)%in%paste(roster$school_year,roster$RBD))]
hist[is.na(RBD),pace_school:=NA_integer_]
saveRDS(hist,file.path(p,'upper_school_history.rds'))
# The full graduating reference population comes from school records, not lotteries or applicants.
grad<-hist[COD_GRADO==4L & passed & AGNO>=2020,.(MRUN,grad_year=AGNO,RBD,pace12=pace_school)]
prev<-hist[COD_GRADO==3L,.(MRUN,grad_year=AGNO+1L,rbd11=RBD,pace11=pace_school)]
grad<-merge(grad,prev,by=c('MRUN','grad_year'),all.x=TRUE)
grad[,school_both:=pace12==1 & pace11==1]
raw<-readRDS(file.path(p,'student_pace_2020_2025.rds'))
raw[,raw_selection:=as.integer(rowSums(as.matrix(.SD)==24,na.rm=TRUE)>0),.SDcols=patterns('^marca_pace_')]
stopifnot(all(raw$assigned_pace == raw$raw_selection))
flag_check <- raw[,.(n=.N, stored_flag=sum(is_pace==1), first_preference=sum(!is.na(marca_pace_1)), flag_first_disagreements=sum((is_pace==1)!=!is.na(marca_pace_1))),by=year]
fwrite(flag_check,file.path(f08_dir,'pace_flag_definition_audit.csv'))
stopifnot(all(flag_check[year>=2023,flag_first_disagreements]==0L))
raw[,record_appearance:=as.integer(rowSums(!is.na(as.matrix(.SD)))>0),.SDcols=patterns('^marca_pace_')]
# Rows without a positive score are unobserved academically, not automatic failures.
raw[ranking<=0,ranking:=NA_integer_]
co<-readRDS(file.path(p,'college_outcomes_2018_2026.rds'));setDT(co)
score_check <- merge(raw[year>=2021,.(mrun,proc=as.integer(year),raw_rank=ranking)],co[,.(mrun,proc,ranking)],by=c('mrun','proc'))
stopifnot(nrow(score_check)==1481303L, score_check[raw_rank>0 & !is.na(ranking),sum(raw_rank!=ranking)]==0L)
rm(score_check)
grad<-merge(grad,co[,.(MRUN=mrun,grad_year=proc-1L,ranking,exam_lm)],by=c('MRUN','grad_year'),all.x=TRUE)
grad<-merge(grad,raw[year>=2021,.(MRUN=mrun,grad_year=as.integer(year)-1L,egreso_yyyy,pace_flag=is_pace,raw_selection,record_appearance,l=lenguaje_actual,m=matematica_actual,h=historia_actual,c=ciencias_actual)],by=c('MRUN','grad_year'),all.x=TRUE)
rules<-fread('analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/f08/pace_rules_2021_2026.csv')
grad<-merge(grad,rules[,.(grad_year=new_graduation_cohort,top_share,minimum_ranking)],by='grad_year',all.x=TRUE)
grad[,absolute:=ranking>=minimum_ranking]
grad[,exams_current:=l>0 & m>0 & (h>0 | c>0)]
# Rank coverage in the relevant full graduating population.
coverage <- grad[,.(graduates=.N, rank_coverage=mean(!is.na(ranking)), pace12=sum(pace12==1,na.rm=TRUE), pace_both=sum(school_both,na.rm=TRUE), history_missing=mean(is.na(school_both))),by=grad_year]
pace_coverage <- grad[school_both==TRUE,.(n=.N, rank_coverage=mean(!is.na(ranking)), flag_n=sum(pace_flag==1,na.rm=TRUE), absolute_rate=mean(absolute,na.rm=TRUE), missing_flag=mean(is.na(pace_flag))),by=grad_year]
fwrite(coverage,file.path(f08_dir,'graduate_score_coverage.csv'))
fwrite(pace_coverage,file.path(f08_dir,'pace_school_score_coverage.csv'))
knitr::kable(coverage)
saveRDS(grad,file.path(p,'graduates_pace_audit.rds'))

```

The absolute-score alternative is directly observed when a valid official Ranking
score is present. The within-school alternative is harder: many graduates,
especially at PACE schools, have no observed Ranking score. `PORC_SUP_NOTAS` is a
GPA percentile and is not substituted for a percentile of the official Ranking
score. Ranking only the observed students would shrink the denominator and can
misclassify applicants. The code therefore produces both a clearly labeled
observed-score proxy and conservative classifications that allow missing scores
to occupy any rank. Ties and noninteger quota sizes are handled conservatively:
a guaranteed pass uses the worst tied rank and the floor of the quota; a definite
failure uses the best tied rank and the ceiling. Boundary cases remain unknown.

The full-class calculation is an independent measure of academic standing at
PACE and non-PACE schools. It is not universally the official eligibility rule:
the 2024 resolution restricts the ranking reference to graduates satisfying the
school-history requirement. A separate school-history-reference calculation is
provided as a sensitivity check, retaining unknown school histories. Neither
calculation is declared to be complete official eligibility without the operational
reference roster, tie rule, and complete scores. The school-history measure uses
records in the scheduled grade-11 and grade-12 years; missing, conflicting, or
nonconsecutive histories are not silently certified as qualifying attendance.

```{r f08-academic-construction}
p <- f08_input
out <- f08_dir
g <- readRDS(file.path(p, "graduates_pace_audit.rds"))
g[, `:=`(n_grad=.N, n_rank=sum(!is.na(ranking)),
          rank_min=frank(-ranking,ties.method="min",na.last="keep"),
          rank_max_observed=frank(-ranking,ties.method="max",na.last="keep")),
  by=.(grad_year,RBD)]
g[, pct_obs := rank_min/n_rank]
g[is.na(RBD), pct_obs := NA_real_]
g[, academic_observed := absolute | pct_obs <= top_share]
g[, `:=`(academic_lower=as.integer((!is.na(absolute) & absolute) |
            (!is.na(ranking) & rank_max_observed+n_grad-n_rank <= floor(top_share*n_grad))),
          academic_upper=as.integer(is.na(ranking) | (!is.na(absolute) & absolute) |
            (!is.na(ranking) & rank_min <= ceiling(top_share*n_grad))))]
g[is.na(RBD), `:=`(academic_lower=as.integer(!is.na(absolute)&absolute),
                    academic_upper=1L)]
g[, academic_partial := fifelse(academic_lower==1L,1L,
                                 fifelse(academic_upper==0L,0L,NA_integer_))]
stopifnot(all(g$academic_lower <= g$academic_upper))
# School-history-restricted reference: unknown histories can enter the denominator
# and, conservatively, rank ahead of a known qualifying student.
g[, `:=`(ref_known=sum(school_both %in% TRUE),
          ref_unknown=sum(is.na(school_both)),
          ref_rank_missing=sum(school_both %in% TRUE & is.na(ranking))),
  by=.(grad_year,RBD)]
g[, `:=`(ref_rank_min=NA_real_,ref_rank_max=NA_real_)]
g[school_both==TRUE, `:=`(
  ref_rank_min=frank(-ranking,ties.method="min",na.last="keep"),
  ref_rank_max=frank(-ranking,ties.method="max",na.last="keep")),by=.(grad_year,RBD)]
g[, history_joint_lower := as.integer(school_both %in% TRUE &
    ((!is.na(absolute) & absolute) | (!is.na(ref_rank_max) &
      ref_rank_max+ref_rank_missing+ref_unknown <= floor(top_share*ref_known))))]
g[, history_joint_upper := as.integer(!(school_both %in% FALSE) &
    (is.na(school_both) | is.na(ranking) | (!is.na(absolute)&absolute) |
      (!is.na(ref_rank_min) & ref_rank_min <= ceiling(top_share*(ref_known+ref_unknown)))))]
g[is.na(RBD), `:=`(history_joint_lower=0L,history_joint_upper=1L)]
stopifnot(all(g$history_joint_lower <= g$history_joint_upper))
classification <- g[,.(graduates=.N,rank_missing=sum(is.na(ranking)),
  academic_guaranteed=sum(academic_lower),academic_possible=sum(academic_upper),
  academic_unresolved=sum(is.na(academic_partial)),
  history_joint_guaranteed=sum(history_joint_lower),
  history_joint_possible=sum(history_joint_upper)),by=grad_year]
fwrite(classification,file.path(out,"academic_classification_coverage.csv"))
# A generous full-graduating-class denominator makes this a diagnostic exclusion;
# it is not a claim to have recovered the official reference population.
g[, definitely_below := academic_upper==0L]
flag_audit <- g[!is.na(pace_flag),.(n=.N,
    flag_n=sum(pace_flag==1),
    flagged_below_even_optimistic_cutoff=sum(pace_flag==1 & definitely_below),
    flagged_missing_rank=sum(pace_flag==1 & is.na(ranking)),
    selected_n=sum(raw_selection==1,na.rm=TRUE),
    selected_below_even_optimistic_cutoff=sum(raw_selection==1 & definitely_below,na.rm=TRUE)),
    by=grad_year]
fwrite(flag_audit,file.path(out,"pace_flag_academic_crosscheck.csv"))
fwrite(g[!is.na(pace_flag),.N,by=.(grad_year,pace_flag,pace12,school_both,
      academic_partial,exams_current,raw_selection)],
      file.path(out,"pace_status_crosstabs.csv"))
saveRDS(g,file.path(p,"graduates_pace_audit.rds"))
knitr::kable(classification)
```

```{r f08-finalized-channel-estimates}
library(data.table);library(fixest)
setDTthreads(4);setFixest_vcov(all='hetero');setFixest_estimation(fixef.rm='none')
p<-'analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/input/f08';out<-'analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/f08'
panel<-as.data.table(readRDS('analysis_for_adversarial_report_output/input/section3_panel.rds'))
controls<-c('GPA8_Z','ES_MUJER','PRIORITARIO','ALTO','ORIGIN_OD')
panel<-panel[LOTTERY_SAMPLE==TRUE & YEAR<=2020 & complete.cases(panel[,..controls])]
panel[,`:=`(proc=YEAR+5L,grad_year=YEAR+4L)]
h<-readRDS(file.path(p,'upper_school_history.rds'))
h11<-h[COD_GRADO==3,.(MRUN,YEAR=AGNO-3L,school11=pace_school,school11_seen=1L,school11_ambiguous=as.integer(n_school!=1))]
h12<-h[COD_GRADO==4,.(MRUN,YEAR=AGNO-4L,school12=pace_school,school12_seen=1L,school12_ambiguous=as.integer(n_school!=1))]
d<-merge(panel,h11,by=c('MRUN','YEAR'),all.x=TRUE);d<-merge(d,h12,by=c('MRUN','YEAR'),all.x=TRUE)

d<-merge(d,co[,.(MRUN=mrun,proc=as.integer(year),stored_pace_flag=is_pace,pace_selection=raw_selection,pace_application=applied_pace,pace_record=record_appearance,raw_ranking=ranking,college_record=1L)],by=c('MRUN','proc'),all.x=TRUE)
g<-readRDS(file.path(p,'graduates_pace_audit.rds'))
d<-merge(d,g[,.(MRUN,grad_year,grad_record=1L,ranking,absolute,academic_observed,pct_obs,school_both,exams_current,n_grad,n_rank,academic_lower,academic_upper,academic_partial,history_joint_lower,history_joint_upper)],by=c('MRUN','grad_year'),all.x=TRUE)
# Full-frame events count absence of a recorded event as zero; eligibility itself stays missing.
for(n in c('school11','school12','school11_seen','school12_seen','school11_ambiguous','school12_ambiguous','stored_pace_flag','pace_selection','pace_application','pace_record','college_record','grad_record'))set(d,j=n,value=as.integer(!is.na(d[[n]]) & d[[n]]==1))
d[,`:=`(school_both_recorded=as.integer(school11==1 & school12==1),rank_observed=as.integer(!is.na(ranking)),absolute_recorded=as.integer(!is.na(absolute)&absolute),academic_proxy_recorded=as.integer(!is.na(academic_observed)&academic_observed),joint_proxy_recorded=as.integer(!is.na(academic_observed)&academic_observed&school11==1&school12==1))]
d[,`:=`(academic_lower_event=fifelse(grad_record==0L,0L,academic_lower),
          academic_upper_event=fifelse(grad_record==0L,0L,academic_upper),
          history_joint_lower_event=fifelse(grad_record==0L,0L,history_joint_lower),
          history_joint_upper_event=fifelse(grad_record==0L,0L,history_joint_upper))]
stopifnot(nrow(d)==131709L,!anyDuplicated(d,by=c('MRUN','YEAR')),
          all(d$pace_selection<=d$pace_application))
# Conditional models are descriptive comparisons in a post-offer selected sample.
fitrow<-function(data,v,label,sample){
 rhs<-paste('i(YEAR, ref=2016) +',paste(controls,collapse=' + '))
 rf<-feols(as.formula(paste(v,'~ OFFER +',rhs,'| CHANCE_GROUP')),data=data)
 iv<-feols(as.formula(paste(v,'~',rhs,'| CHANCE_GROUP | D_OD ~ OFFER')),data=data,ssc=ssc(K.adj=FALSE))
 fs<-feols(as.formula(paste('D_OD ~ OFFER +',rhs,'| CHANCE_GROUP')),data=data)
 rbindlist(lapply(list(rf=rf,iv=iv),function(m){term<-if('fit_D_OD'%in%names(coef(m)))'fit_D_OD' else 'OFFER';se1<-se(m)[[term]];b<-coef(m)[[term]];data.table(outcome=v,label=label,sample=sample,estimator=if(term=='fit_D_OD')'IV attendance' else 'RF offer',estimate_pp=b*100,se_pp=se1*100,lower_pp=(b-1.96*se1)*100,upper_pp=(b+1.96*se1)*100,p=if(term=='fit_D_OD')2*pnorm(-abs(b/se1)) else pvalue(m)[[term]],n=nobs(m),control_mean=mean(data[OFFER==0][[v]],na.rm=TRUE)*100,first_stage=coef(fs)[['OFFER']])}))
}
vars<-c(pace_selection='Recorded PACE selection',pace_application='Recorded PACE application',pace_record='Any PACE preference-status record',stored_pace_flag='Stored PACE label (definition changes)',school11='Recorded PACE-school attendance in scheduled grade 11',school12='Recorded PACE-school attendance in scheduled grade 12',school_both_recorded='Recorded PACE-school attendance in both scheduled grades',school11_seen='Any scheduled grade-11 record',school12_seen='Any scheduled grade-12 record',school11_ambiguous='Multiple scheduled grade-11 schools',school12_ambiguous='Multiple scheduled grade-12 schools',grad_record='Recorded on-time youth graduation',rank_observed='Ranking observed for on-time graduate',absolute_recorded='On-time graduate with observed Ranking above annual cutoff',academic_proxy_recorded='Observed academic OR proxy (incomplete ranking reference)',joint_proxy_recorded='School history and observed academic proxy',academic_lower_event='Academic classification: guaranteed-pass endpoint',academic_upper_event='Academic classification: possible-pass endpoint',history_joint_lower_event='School-history-reference joint lower endpoint',history_joint_upper_event='School-history-reference joint upper endpoint')
results<-rbindlist(lapply(names(vars),function(v)fitrow(d,v,vars[[v]],'Full lottery frame, SAE 2016-2020')))
cond<-d[!is.na(ranking)]
results<-rbindlist(list(results,fitrow(cond,'absolute','Absolute Ranking threshold','On-time graduates with Ranking observed'),fitrow(cond,'academic_observed','Academic OR proxy','On-time graduates with Ranking observed')))
fwrite(results,file.path(out,'pace_new_estimates.csv'))
fwrite(d[,.(n=.N,pace_selected=sum(pace_selection),school_both=mean(school_both_recorded),rank_observed=mean(rank_observed),absolute_recorded=mean(absolute_recorded)),by=.(YEAR,OFFER)],file.path(out,'pace_panel_coverage.csv'))
saveRDS(d,file.path(p,'pace_finalized_panel.rds'))
knitr::kable(results[outcome %in% c('pace_selection','school_both_recorded','rank_observed','absolute','academic_observed'),.(label,sample,estimator,estimate_pp,se_pp,lower_pp,upper_pp,n)])

```

The endpoint regressions above are sensitivity calculations, not causal effect
bounds: regression weights can have both signs. The next chunk uses those signs
to compute the range of the fitted offer coefficient over every completion of
unresolved binary classifications. This is an identification diagnostic for the
sample coefficient, not a confidence interval or a complete partial-identification
inference procedure. It does not solve uncertainty about the official reference
population or missing selection-route data in 2026.

```{r f08-classification-sensitivity}
rhs <- paste('i(YEAR, ref=2016) +',paste(controls,collapse=' + '))
z <- resid(feols(as.formula(paste('OFFER ~',rhs,'| CHANCE_GROUP')),data=d))
w <- z/sum(z*d$OFFER)
fs <- coef(feols(as.formula(paste('D_OD ~ OFFER +',rhs,'| CHANCE_GROUP')),data=d))[["OFFER"]]
completion_range <- function(low,high,label) {
  stopifnot(!anyNA(low),!anyNA(high),all(low<=high))
  lo <- sum(w*ifelse(w>=0,low,high))
  hi <- sum(w*ifelse(w>=0,high,low))
  data.table(definition=label,unresolved=sum(low!=high),n=nrow(d),
             rf_min_pp=100*lo,rf_max_pp=100*hi,
             iv_min_pp=100*lo/fs,iv_max_pp=100*hi/fs)
}
ranges <- rbindlist(list(
 completion_range(d$academic_lower_event,d$academic_upper_event,
                  "Independent full-class academic standing"),
 completion_range(d$history_joint_lower_event,d$history_joint_upper_event,
                  "School-history-reference joint sensitivity")))
fwrite(ranges,file.path(out,"academic_completion_ranges.csv"))
# Check the linear weighting representation against an ordinary fitted effect.
stopifnot(abs(sum(w*d$pace_selection)*100 -
 results[outcome=='pace_selection' & estimator=='RF offer',estimate_pp]) < 1e-8)
knitr::kable(ranges)
```

```{r f08-review-report}
line_effect <- function(v,est="RF offer") {
 r <- results[outcome==v & estimator==est]
 stopifnot(nrow(r)==1L)
 sprintf("%s pp (95%% CI [%s, %s]; N=%s)",fmt(r$estimate_pp),
   fmt(r$lower_pp),fmt(r$upper_pp),format(r$n,big.mark=",",trim=TRUE))
}

 paste0("- Offer effect on recorded PACE selection: ",line_effect("pace_selection"),"."),

Operational confirmation of the reference roster, ties and rounding is still needed, as are official Ranking scores for unobserved graduates. Nonconsecutive school histories, adult-education graduation, and missing/ambiguous school records are not certified as eligible. Required exams are checked when observed; unused carryover cannot be inferred solely from current-year scores, and these new models deliberately focus on the on-time process rather than claim a complete ever-eligible reconstruction.",
 "The MRUN-linked 2026 extract does not preserve the admission route. Do not code that year as zero PACE admissions. Extend the common sample only when its original route records are available.", "",
 "The results establish lower recorded PACE selection and lower recorded PACE-school attendance. Academic scores provide evidence consistent with a second channel, but the current data do not identify a complete academic-eligibility effect or the share of the admission effect mediated by either channel. F08.3 stays open. The manuscript's existing empirical tables have not been replaced with provisional eligibility estimates.", "",
 "## Sources and reproducibility", "",
 "- Ministry PACE document registry: https://dfi.mineduc.cl/instrumentos-de-financiamiento/asignacion-directa/programa-pace/",
 "- Annual school directories: https://datosabiertos.mineduc.cl/directorio-de-establecimientos-educacionales/",
 "- Official annual guides/resolutions and source URLs: `sources/`, `pace_rules_2021_2026.csv`.",
 "- School roster and correction log: `sources/schools/official_pace_schools_2019_2025.csv`, `sources/schools/ocr_corrections.csv`.",
 "- Upstream source: `archive/1_data_processing_upstream.Rmd`, lines 294–342, 1102–1105, 1351–1353.",
 "- Original P167 dictionary: `sources/dictionaries/20220420_Diccionario de variables Actualizado 2022.xlsx`, sheet 1 rows 363 and 369.",
 "- All new statistical code: `analysis_for_adversarial_report.Rmd`, chunks `f08-*`. The Python helper performs only memory-bounded RDS projection.",
 "- Aggregate estimates and coverage: `pace_new_estimates.csv`, `pace_panel_coverage.csv`, `graduate_score_coverage.csv`, `pace_school_score_coverage.csv`, `academic_classification_coverage.csv`, `pace_status_crosstabs.csv`.")
writeLines(report,file.path(out,"pace_findings_2026-10-19.md"))
# Input and source checksums contain paths and hashes only, not student identifiers.
source_files <- list.files(file.path(out,"sources"),recursive=TRUE,full.names=TRUE)
source_files <- source_files[!file.info(source_files)$isdir]
fwrite(data.table(path=source_files,md5=unname(tools::md5sum(source_files))),
       file.path(out,"source_manifest.csv"))

  "panel_performance_2002_2023.rds","rendimiento_grades_2024_2025.rds",
  "college_outcomes_2018_2026.rds","paes_2026.rds"))

                 md5=unname(tools::md5sum(input_files))),file.path(out,"input_manifest.csv"))
cat(paste(report[1:18],collapse="\n"))
```

F08.2 is documented at the variable-source level. F08.3 remains open until the
unresolved academic classifications and 2026 route coverage are resolved. The
current results support the PACE-school channel; they do not establish a causal
mediation decomposition between school participation and academic qualification.

## Environment

The local package versions need not match the handoff's Windows environment.
The numerical reproduction checks above establish whether the existing results
match at the precision reported in the current tables.
